summary: Among genuinely untrained young men, between-person variability in absolute 1RM is moderate in small homogeneous study samples (CV ~12-15% for bench and leg press, e.g. sedentary men bench 125 +/- 18 lb at 166 lb BW, ~0.73x BW), but population norms show a much wider spread: Cooper Institute bench/BW norms for men 20-29 run from 0.72x (p5) to 1.63x (p95), i.e. roughly SD ~0.25-0.3x BW around a median ~1.0x, and those norms come from a fitter-than-average clinic sample. Training response is large and very heterogeneous: ~20-21% (+/-11.5%, range -8 to +60%) after ~5 months in 287 untrained adults (Ahtiainen 2016), 0 to +250% for 12 weeks of arm training in 585 people (Hubal 2005), and 10-20% of early 'gains' in novices is just 1RM-test familiarisation. Once competitive, powerlifters still add ~7.5-12.5% in their first competitive year and ~20% more over 10 years (Latella), so a multi-year trained lifter is plausibly ~1.5-2.5x an untrained person's 1RM, though no source gives clean 1/3/5-year percentages and Kraemer's commonly quoted tiered percentages were not confirmed. ExRx 'Untrained' (a sedentary-but-healthy floor, not a median) is ~0.65-0.74x BW for bench (e.g. 128 lb at 181 lb BW) and ~0.8x for deadlift (150 lb at 181 lb); a 2x bodyweight bench is ~p95+ among app-logging lifters and, by inference from general-population norms, likely above the 99th percentile of all men.
